concepts.title: How State and Society Organised Themselves

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'How State and Society Organised Themselves' refers to.
questions.a: Before 1000 CE Indian society organised itself through kingdoms, varna-based social order and village communities: rulers collected taxes and protected land, Brahmanas, chiefs and guilds held influence, and local assemblies managed everyday affairs in many regions.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'How State and Society Organised Themselves'.
questions.a: King, community and custom together ran early states - power was shared, not absolute.

questions.q: Under which section is 'How State and Society Organised Themselves' taught, and from which source text?

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Land, Revenue and Grants' refers to.
questions.a: Land was the backbone of the early economy: peasants produced grain, a share went to the ruler as tax, and kings made land grants to Brahmanas and temples recorded on copper plates - grants that also pushed agriculture into new areas.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Land, Revenue and Grants'.
questions.a: Land fed the state; land grants bound kings, priests and temples in one economy.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Land, Revenue and Grants' taught, and from which source text?

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Trade, Cities and Cultural Life' refers to.
questions.a: Guilds of merchants and craftspeople, busy port and inland cities, coinage and temple towns marked the economic vigour of the age, while Sanskrit, Prakrit and Tamil literatures, temples and philosophy enriched its cultural life up to 1000 CE.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Trade, Cities and Cultural Life'.
questions.a: Trade fed cities, cities fed culture: economy and ideas grew together.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Trade, Cities and Cultural Life' taught, and from which source text?
